I'll show the exact jsonPath keys to use, why the current assertions fail, and give corrected assertion examples you can paste into the testChecklist

 to avoid further failures.

Why your current assertions fail
- In `PaceDto` the fields are named `minutes` and `unit` (not `PaceUnit`). The JSON for pace will therefore use "minutes" and "unit".
- The test tries to assert the enum value using the enum constant object (`PaceUnit.PER_MILE`) instead of the serialized string (e.g. "PER_MILE"). Use the enum name (string) or a Hamcrest matcher.
- Some of your tests assert the wrong index / wrong names (e.g., you create "Row" but assert "Swim" — watch indices).

JSON shape produced for `CardioExerciseDto`
Example JSON for one cardio item:
{
  "id": 1,
  "name": "Jog",
  "durationMinutes": 20.0,
  "caloriesBurned": 200,
  "pace": {
    "minutes": 10.0,
    "unit": "PER_MILE"
  }
}

Correct jsonPath usage
- Pace minutes: $.pace.minutes (for a single object) or $[0].pace.minutes (for an array element)
- Pace unit (enum string): $.pace.unit or $[0].pace.unit

Corrected MockMvc assertions

1) For a single-object response (GET /api/cardio/{id} or GET /api/cardio/name/{name}):
.andExpect(jsonPath("$.pace.minutes").value(10.0))
.andExpect(jsonPath("$.pace.unit").value(PaceUnit.PER_MILE.name()))

or using a literal string:
.andExpect(jsonPath("$.pace.unit").value("PER_MILE"))

or using Hamcrest:
import static org.hamcrest.Matchers.is);
...
.andExpect(jsonPath("$.pace.unit", is(PaceUnit.PER_MILE.name())))

2) For an array response (GET /api/cardio) — for the first element:
.andExpect(jsonPath("$[0].pace.minutes").value(10.0))
.andExpect(jsonPath("$[0].pace.unit").value(PaceUnit.PER_MILE.name()))

and for the second element:
.andExpect(jsonPath("$[1].pace.minutes").value(2.1))
.andExpect(jsonPath("$[1].pace.unit").value(PaceUnit.PER_500M.name()))

Concrete corrected block (replace the problematic block around lines 163–173):

Notes and tips
- Use .name() on enum constants so the test compares to the string produced by Jackson.
- For numeric comparisons prefer numeric literals (10.0, 20.0) instead of strings.
- If Jackson is configured to serialize enums as a different form (e.g., lowercase), adapt assertions accordingly — by default it uses the enum name (UPPER_SNAKE_CASE here).
- If you prefer stronger typed assertions, import Hamcrest Matchers and use e.g. jsonPath("$[0].pace.unit", is(PaceUnit.PER_MILE.name())).
